subject: Calendar vs fiscal coverage — clarification and evidence request
messages:
From: Dana Kline <dana.k@harper-audits.com>
To: rachel.kim@redwood.com
Cc: tasks@harper-audits.com
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Question on audit coverage alignment (calendar vs fiscal)

Hi Rachel,

Quick question while we prep for the SOC 2 Type II review for AcmeHealth: your team provided monthly snapshots, but the client’s accounting is on a fiscal-month schedule (ends on the 25th). For our evidence mapping we need to confirm whether Redwood treats the reported "monthly" snapshots as calendar-month (1st–30/31st) or aligned to a customer-specified fiscal month. Specifically: 

- Do your automated snapshot/backup processes use calendar boundaries by default?
- If a customer requests a fiscal alignment (e.g., 26th–25th), can you produce point-in-time snapshots that follow that window, and if so, how are those labeled in your evidence manifests?

If you can point me to any example evidence naming conventions or a short note that we can attach to the auditor file, that would be great. Also please indicate whether partial-month activity (e.g., a new service deployed on the 20th) is included in your monthly coverage or treated as a separate point-in-time artifact.

Thanks,
Dana Kline
Senior Manager, Harper Audits
Demand: SOC 2 Type II — AcmeHealth

[attachment: requested-evidence-manifest-template.csv]

From: rachel.kim@redwood.com
To: Dana Kline <dana.k@harper-audits.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Question on audit coverage alignment (calendar vs fiscal)

Dana —

Thanks for the clear callout. Short answer: our platform captures calendar-month snapshots by default, and we can produce fiscal-aligned snapshots on request. A few details below so the evidence package is explicit for your mapping: 

- Default behavior: automated daily checkpointing, with a monthly aggregate snapshot labeled YYYY-MM (calendar month). These live in our snapshot store and the manifest uses the calendar boundaries.
- Fiscal alignment: we support customer-specific windows. When requested, we generate a point-in-time snapshot for the fiscal boundary (e.g., 2026-10-25T23:59:59Z for a 26th–25th fiscal month). Those are emitted as separate artifacts named fiscal-YYYY-MM-DD-TO-YYYY-MM-DD and included in the manifest with the label "fiscal-aligned".
- Partial-month events: included in both the nearest calendar snapshot and as part of the fiscal-aligned artifact if that window is requested. We also keep the underlying transaction logs (append-only) so the auditor can reconcile events that span transitions.

I attached a small manifest export and a draft of a bridge-letter paragraph you can include that explains naming conventions. I’m looping in Marissa and Ben to confirm two operational points: retention of the underlying transaction logs for cross-boundary reconciliations, and whether we can produce a CSV of event counts by customer-specific window.

Next steps: 
- If you confirm the exact fiscal boundaries AcmeHealth needs, we’ll queue production of the fiscal-aligned artifacts and provide a signed bridge-letter.
- We can provide a reconciler CSV and the underlying log retention policy within 48 hours of request.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Head of Trust & Safety, Redwood Inference
Mobile: (415) 555-0183

[attachment: requested-evidence-manifest.csv]

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: rachel.kim@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Cc: soojin.lee@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 08:37:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Question on audit coverage alignment (calendar vs fiscal)

Looping in Soojin (systems) — operational notes below for the auditor thread: 

- Retention: transaction logs (immutable append-only) are retained 13 months by default for hosted accounts; we can extend to 25 months on request (usually for enterprise).
- Snapshots: daily checkpoints are stored as chunked MV snapshots. Calendar-month aggregates are compiled on the 1st of the following month (00:00 UTC) and tagged calendar-YYYY-MM. Fiscal-aligned artifacts are created on-demand and include a full manifest plus index (redwood-snapshot-index.json).
- Naming and proof: fiscal-aligned artifacts include a signed manifest entry (SHA256) and a timestamped wrapper with service instance IDs. We can include a docu-sign style attestation (bridge letter) and attach the draft.

Operational asks for Rachel/Dana: please specify the fiscal boundary (start/end dates) and whether AcmeHealth needs a single one-off artifact or monthly recurring fiscal artifacts. Ben, please advise on whether there are cost implications for repeated on-demand fiscal snapshots — I recall a minor billable job for repeated extra exports.

-M

Marissa Cole
Director, Security Assurance
Redwood Inference

From: rachel.kim@redwood.com
To: Dana Kline <dana.k@harper-audits.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, soojin.lee@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 14:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Question on audit coverage alignment (calendar vs fiscal)

Dana —

Thanks, all. Confirming the request from AcmeHealth: fiscal months are 26th–25th. Please accept the attached bridge-letter draft we’ll sign once you confirm. We will: 

- Produce a one-off set of fiscal-aligned snapshots for the prior 12 months (26th–25th windows) and provide: the fiscal artifact (fiscal-YYYY-26-TO-YYYY-MM-25), the reconciler CSV (event counts), and the signed manifest with SHA256 checksums.
- Provide the underlying transaction log exports for reconciliation (13-month retention included). If AcmeHealth requires longer retention, we’ll quote the extension.
- Include a brief paragraph in the bridge letter explaining naming conventions and our default calendar-month behavior.

Please confirm acceptance of the draft (attached) and whether Acme would like monthly recurring fiscal artifacts going forward or only the historical 12 months. Once you confirm, we’ll schedule the export job (estimated 24–36 hours for the initial package) and route the signed bridge-letter back to Harper Audits.

Best regards,
Rachel
Head of Trust & Safety, Redwood Inference
